explanation: Requested eta point (W=1.7 GeV, Q2=1.0 GeV^2, cos theta*=0, phi*=90 deg) is kinematically fine: W is well above the p-eta threshold (~1.486 GeV) and the kinematics are otherwise unremarkable, so I generated the input file with vcut set to -0.1 as asked. However, I checked the actual Fortran logic in eta/exclurad.F (subroutine bornkin, line ~254): 'if(cutv.gt.1d-12)vmax=min(vmax,cutv)'. This means any vcut <= 1e-12 -- including 0 and any negative value -- fails the test and the inelasticity cut is simply not applied; vmax falls back to its natural kinematic bound. The README.md and examples/README.md in this repo describe a negative vcut as 'a cut on v directly rather than v^2', but that behavior is not implemented anywhere in exclurad.F or fint.F for either the eta or pion configurations (I checked both). So running this input will produce results numerically identical to vcut=0 (no inelasticity cut at all), not the documented alternate cut mode. I generated the file exactly as requested (vcut = -0.1) rather than silently changing it, so you can reproduce this behavior yourself, but you should be aware the documentation and the code disagree here -- treat vcut=-0.1 as equivalent to 'no cut' unless the source is patched to add the missing negative-vcut branch.
